whoWeAre.heading: One Ummah,
whoWeAre.p1: The Rwanda Muslim Community (RMC), formerly AMUR, represents Muslims in Rwanda, whose history spans over a century. Islam was introduced in the late 19th century by Swahili traders from the East African coast, spreading gradually among urban and marginalized communities. During German and Belgian colonial rule, Muslims faced discrimination, exclusion from education and employment, and social marginalization.
whoWeAre.p2: After independence in 1962, Muslims remained a small minority and largely stayed away from ethnic divisions, emphasizing religious unity. During the Rwandan Genocide, Muslim leaders condemned violence, promoted unity, and mosques served as places of refuge, shaping a positive perception of Islam afterward.
whoWeAre.point1: Present in all 5 provinces and 30 districts
whoWeAre.point3: Faith, education, and welfare under one roof
whoWeAre.p3: In the post-genocide period, Islam experienced steady growth due to increased freedom, equality, and openness, allowing Muslims to share their faith widely. Today, Muslims make up about 5–10% of Rwanda’s population, are well integrated into society, and actively contribute to interfaith dialogue and national unity. The community is currently led by Mufti Sheikh SINDAYIGAYA Musa, who oversees religious affairs and representation.

f1.q: Do I need an account to apply?
f1.a: Yes. Signing in lets us contact you and lets you track your application from start to decision.

f2.q: What file types and sizes can I upload?
f2.a: PDF, Word documents and images (JPG or PNG). Each field shows its maximum size, and files are checked before they upload.

f3.q: What if I don't have a good-conduct certificate number?
f3.a: No problem — you can upload a scan or photo of the certificate instead of entering a number.

f4.q: How do I check my application status?
f4.a: Open the "Check status" page and sign in. You'll see each stage: submitted, under review, shortlisted and the final decision.

donate.sectionSub: Explore each category below and add any cause to your gift.

header.intro: Begin with your niyyah — the intention behind your gift — then choose where it goes. Every contribution is transparent and amāna.

lillah.label: Lillah
lillah.desc: Purely for the sake of Allah

quickGive.title: Give where it's needed most
quickGive.subtitle: Know your amount? Add it in one tap — RMC directs it to the greatest need.

school.title: School Related
school.long: Open the doors of knowledge for the next generation — from Qur'an classes to university scholarships for talented students who cannot afford the fees.

charity.title: Charity
charity.desc: Feeding the hungry & supporting the poor.
charity.long: Direct relief for the most vulnerable — food parcels for struggling families, care for orphans, and medical aid for those who would otherwise go without.

religious.title: Religious
religious.long: Sustain the houses of Allah and those who serve them — mosque maintenance, support for imams, and Qur'ans placed in the hands of the community.

events.title: Events
events.long: Bring the ummah together — fund the gatherings that strengthen faith and community, from Eid celebrations to youth camps and national competitions.

scholarship.label: Scholarship Fund
scholarship.long: Full and partial scholarships for bright students from low-income families, covering the cost of staying in school through to graduation.

madrassa.label: Madrassa & Books
madrassa.long: Equip Qur'an schools across the provinces with the books and materials children need to learn to read and memorise the Qur'an.

teachers.label: Teacher Support
teachers.long: Stipends and training for the teachers and du'āt who dedicate their lives to educating the community.

foodbank.label: Food Bank
foodbank.long: Monthly food parcels of staple goods for families facing hardship, with extra support during Ramadan.

orphans.label: Orphan Sponsorship
orphans.long: Sponsor an orphan's essential needs so they can grow up with dignity, nourishment and an education.

medical.label: Medical Aid
medical.long: Cover the cost of consultations, medicine and urgent treatment for those who cannot afford care.

masjid.label: Masjid Maintenance
masjid.long: Keep mosques clean, lit and in good repair — from utility bills to roofing and wudu facilities.

imam.label: Imam Support
imam.long: Stipends, training and outreach support for the imams who lead prayer and serve their communities.

quran.label: Qur'an Distribution
quran.long: Print and distribute mushafs so every household and mosque has access to the Book of Allah.

e1.title: Eid al-Adha National Celebration
e1.long: Host the national Eid al-Adha celebration — prayer, qurbani and a shared meal that brings thousands of believers together.

e2.title: RMC Annual Scholarship Awards Ceremony
e2.long: Celebrate and fund the next cohort of RMC scholars at the annual awards ceremony, recognising academic excellence.

e3.title: Muslim Women Leadership Summit
e3.long: Empower Muslim women through a leadership summit of workshops, mentorship and networking across the country.

e4.title: Qur'an Recitation Competition — National Finals
e4.long: Stage the national finals of the Qur'an recitation competition, honouring the huffāz of Rwanda.

e5.title: RMC General Assembly Meeting
e5.long: Support the running of RMC's General Assembly — the governance gathering that steers the community's work.
